answer: A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The dune multiplier is published, charged in cipher, and lotus lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 8 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 2448 identities would post 3088 proofs and burn roughly 21 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
